title: Culture, Marriage, Family & Kinship
content: Dear EthioFresh Family! Welcome to the complete, exam-destroying ultimate study guide for Social Anthropology Chapter 3 (3.7 - 3.9)! 🚀✨ No need to stress or open any other book—everything you need for a solid 100% in your exams is fully broken down right here line-by-line in perfect order directly from your module! Grab your favorite beverage, relax, and let's conquer this together! 📚🔥 --- 3.7 Ties That Connect: Marriage, Family and Kinship 3.7.1 Marriage * There is no one universally applicable definition of marriage, because the Cross Cultural Variability in the existence of rare forms of marriage in specific societies renders such definitions invalid. * A commonly quoted definition comes from Notes and Queries in Anthropology: "Marriage is a union between a man and a woman such that the children born to the woman are recognized as legitimate offspring of both partners" (Royal Anthropological Institute, 1951). * This definition isn't universally valid for several reasons: 1. Marriages may unite more than two spouses (plural marriages). 2. Fraternal Polyandry: A woman weds a group of brothers—an arrangement that is characteristic of certain Himalayan cultures. 3. Some societies, including the modern nations of Belgium and the Netherlands, recognize same sex marriages. 4. Traditionally in Africa’s Sudan, a Nuer woman could marry another woman if her father had only daughters but no male heirs, who are necessary if his patrilineage is to survive. He might ask his daughter to stand as a son in order to take a bride. 5. This was a symbolic and social relationship rather than a sexual one. This woman's 'wife' had sex with a man or men (whom her female 'husband' had to approve) until she got pregnant. 6. The children born to the wife were accepted as the offspring of both husband and wife. Although the female husband was not the actual genitor (biological father) of the children, she was their pater (socially recognized father) (Kottak, 2005). 7. The Nayar of Southern India: Did not have marriage in the conventional sense of the term. Although teenage Nayar girls took a ritual husband in a public ceremony, the husband took no responsibility for the woman after the ceremony, and frequently he never saw her again. Thus the Nayar do not have marriage according to our definition in that there is no economic cooperation, regulation of sexual activity, cohabitation, or expectation of permanency. 👉 Marriage (ጋብቻ) አጽናፈ ዓለማዊ (universal) የሆነ አንድ ወጥ ብያኔ የለውም፤ ምክንያቱም በየባህሉ የሚደረጉ የጋብቻ ዓይነቶች በጣም ይለያያሉ። የሮያል አንትሮፖሎጂ ኢንስቲትዩት ብያኔ በብዙ ምክንያቶች አይሰራም፦ ለምሳሌ በሂማላያ Fraternal polyandry (ሴቷ የባልየውን ወንድሞች በሙሉ ታገባለች)፣ በሱዳን ኑኤር (Nuer) ብሔር ደግሞ የወንድ ልጅ የሌለው አባት የዘር ሐረጉ እንዳይቋረጥ ሴት ልጁን እንደ ወንድ አድርጎ ሌላ ሴት ያገበላታል (Female Husband)። እዚህ ጋር እሷ ማህበራዊ አባት (Pater) እንጂ ባዮሎጂካል አባት (Genitor) አይደለችም። በደቡብ ሕንድ ናያር (Nayar) ደግሞ የይስሙላ የሰርግ ሥነ-ሥርዓት ይደረጋል እንጂ አብሮ መኖርና የኢኮኖሚ ትብብር የለም። 💡 Exam Hint: በፈተና ላይ 'Pater' (Social father) እና 'Genitor' (Biological father) ልዩነትን በደቂቃ ውሰዱና ያዙት! 🎯 (ጋብቻ እኮ የፊዚክስ ያህል ሊወሳሰብ ይችላል! 😅) --- 3.7.1.1 Rules of Marriage * Societies have rules that state whom one can and cannot marry. * Every society known to anthropology has established for itself some type of rules regulating mating (sexual intercourse). * The most common form of prohibition is mating with certain type of kin that are defined by the society as being inappropriate sexual partners. * This prohibition on mating with certain categories of relatives is known as incest taboo. * The most universal form of incest taboo involves mating between members of the immediate (nuclear) family: mother-sons, father-daughters, and brother-sisters. * There are a few striking examples of marriage between members of the immediate family that violate the universality of the incest taboo: For political, religious, or economic reasons, members of the royal families among the ancient Egyptians, Incas, and Hawaiians were permitted to mate with and marry their siblings, although this practice did not extend to the ordinary members of those societies. * Marriage is, therefore, a permanent legal union between a man and a woman. It is an important institution without which the society could never be sustained. 👉 Incest Taboo (የቅርብ ዘመድን የማግባት/የመገናኘት ክልከላ) በማንኛውም ማህበረሰብ ውስጥ ከቅርብ የቤተሰብ አባላት (እናት-ልጅ፣ አባት-ልጅ፣ ወንድምና እህት) ጋር የፆታ ግንኙነት ማድረግ ወይም ማገባት በጥብቅ የተከለከለ ነው። ልዩ ሁኔታዎች (Exceptions) የነበሩት በጥንታዊ የግብፅ፣ የኢንካ እና የሃዋይ ንጉሣውያን ቤተሰቦች (Royal families) ውስጥ ብቻ ነበር። 💡 Exam Hint: "Royal families of Ancient Egypt/Inca/Hawaii are exceptions to the Incest Taboo." የሚለው True/False ላይ ይመጣል። --- 3.7.1.2 Mate Selection: Whom Should You Marry? a) Exogamy * This is the rule by which a man is not allowed to marry someone from his own social group. * Such prohibited union is designated as incest. Incest is often considered as sin. * Reasons for exogamy approval: 1. A conception of blood relation prevails among members of a group; marriage within group members is considered a marriage between a brother and sister. 2. Attraction between a male and female gets lost due to close relationship in a small group. 3. There is a popular idea that a great increase of energy and vigor is possible in the progeny if marriage binds two extremely distant persons who possess no kin relation among them. 4. Kottak claimed also that exogamy has adaptive value, because it links people into a wider social network that nurtures, helps, and protects them in times of need pushing social organization outward, establishing and preserving alliances among groups. b) Endogamy * A rule of endogamy requires individuals to marry within their own group and forbids them to marry outside it. * Religious groups such as the Amish, Mormons, Catholics, and Jews have rules of endogamy, though these are often violated when marriage takes place outside the group. * Castes in India and Nepal are also endogamous. * “Indeed, most cultures are endogamous units, although they usually do not need a formal rule requiring people to marry someone from their own society” (Kottak, 2017). c) Preferential Cousin Marriage * Kinship systems based on lineages distinguish between two different types of first cousins: * Cross Cousins: Children of siblings of the opposite sex—that is one’s mother’s brothers’ children and one’s father’s sisters’ children. Most common form because it functions to strengthen and maintain ties between kin groups established in the preceding generation. * Parallel Cousins: When marriage takes place between the children of the siblings of the same sex (mother’s sister’s children and father’s brother’s children). A much less common form found among some Arabic societies in North Africa (marriage of a man to his father's brother's daughter) to prevent the fragmentation of family property. d) The Levirate and Sororate * Rules that require a person to marry the husband or widow of a deceased kin: * The Levirate: Custom whereby a widow is expected to marry the brother (or some close male relative) of her dead husband. Usually any children fathered by the woman’s new husband are considered to belong legally to the dead brother rather than to the actual genitor. Serves as social security for the widow and preserves rights of her husband's family. * The Sororate: Practice of a widower’s marrying the sister (or some close female relative) of his deceased wife. If the deceased spouse has no sibling, the family is obligated to supply a substitute relative (e.g., daughter of deceased wife's brother). 👉 * Exogamy (ከቡድን ውጭ ማገባት)፡ ከራስ ጎሣ/ቤተሰብ ውጭ ማገባት። ጥቅሙ ማህበራዊ ቁርኝትንና ወዳጅነትን ከሌሎች ቡድኖች ጋር ለማስፋት ይረዳል (Adaptive Value)። * Endogamy (በቡድን ውስጥ ማገባት)፡ ከራስ ሃይማኖት፣ ብሔር ወይም የሙያ ስብስብ/Caste ውጭ አለማገባት። * Cross Cousins: የየእናት ወንድም ልጅ ወይም የየአባት እህት ልጅ። * Parallel Cousins: የየአባት ወንድም ልጅ ወይም የየእናት እህት ልጅ። * Levirate (ወንድም አጋቢነት)፡ ባል ሲሞት ሚስትየው የባልን ወንድም የምታገባበት ልማድ። * Sororate (እህት አጋቢነት)፡ ሚስት ስትሞት ባልየው የሟች ሚስቱን እህት የሚያገባበት ልማድ። 💡 Exam Hint: Levirate = Widow + Husband's brother; Sororate = Widower + Wife's sister! በፈተና እንዳትሸወዱ! 😉 --- 3.7.1.3 Number of Spouses * Monogamy: The marriage of one man to one woman at a time. * Polygamy: Marriage of a man or woman with two or more mates. Two types: * Polygyny: The marriage of a man to two or more women at a time. * Sororal Polygyny: Marriage of a man with two or more sisters at a time. * Non-sororal Polygyny: Co-wives are not sisters. * Polyandry: The marriage of a woman to two or more men at a time (practiced in Tibet, Nepal, and India). * Serial Monogamy: Practiced in North America where divorce is common—individuals have more than one spouse, but never legally at the same time. According to Leach, Marriage can accomplish the following (Kottak, 2002): 1. Establish the legal father of a woman's children and legal mother of a man's. 2. Give either or both spouses' rights to the labor of the other. 3. Give either or both spouses a monopoly in the sexuality of the other. 4. Give either or both spouses rights over the other's property. 5. Establish a joint fund of property a partnership for the benefit of the children. 6. Establish a socially significant relationship. 👉 የትዳር አጋር ብዛት ደንቦች፦ Monogamy (አንድ ለአንድ)፣ Polygyny (አንድ ወንድ ብዙ ሚስቶች)፣ Polyandry (አንዲት ሴት ብዙ ባሎች)፣ እና Serial Monogamy (በየተራ ማግባትና መፋታት) ናቸው። --- 3.7.1.4 Economic Consideration of Marriage * Most societies view marriage as a binding contract accompanied by the transfer of economic considerations in four categories: 1. Bridewealth: Compensation given upon marriage by the family of the groom to the family of the bride. According to Murdock (1967), in Africa it was estimated that 82% of societies require payment of bridewealth (often cattle). Functions as security/insurance for good treatment of the wife, stabilizes marriage by reducing divorce, and compensates the bride's lineage for the loss of her economic potential and childbearing capacity. 2. Dowry: Involves a transfer of goods or money from the bride's family to the groom's family. Best known in India but also practiced in Europe; correlates with lower female status where women are perceived as economic burdens. 3. Bride Service: Men give their labor to the bride's family instead of material goods (found in ~14% of societies, e.g., Yanomamo of Venezuela where the groom lives with the bride's parents and hunts for them). 4. Reciprocal Exchange: Found in ~6% of societies (e.g., traditional Vugusu of western Kenya), involving roughly equal exchange of gifts between the families of both bride and groom. 👉 የጋብቻ ኢኮኖሚያዊ ክፍያዎች፦ * Bridewealth (የሙሽራው ቤተሰብ ለሙሽሪት ቤተሰብ የሚሰጠው - ጥያቅ/እጅ መንሻ)። * Dowry (የሙሽሪት ቤተሰብ ለሙሽራው የሚሰጠው - በሕንድ የተለመደ)። * Bride Service (በጉልበት ማገልገል - ለምሳሌ አርሶ ወይም አድኖ ማቅረብ)። * Reciprocal Exchange (እኩል ስጦታ መለዋወጥ)። --- 3.7.1.5 Post-Marital Residence * Patrilocal Residence: Married couple lives with or near relatives of husband's father (69% of societies). * Matrilocal Residence: Married couple lives with or near relatives of the wife (13% of societies). * Avunculocal Residence: Married couple lives with or near husband's mother's brother (4% of societies). * Ambilocal (Bilocal) Residence: Married couple has a choice of living with relatives of wife or husband (9% of societies). * Neolocal Residence: Married couple forms an independent place of residence away from relatives of either spouse (5% of societies). 👉 ከሰርግ በኋላ መኖሪያ ቦታ፦ ባል አባት ጋር (Patrilocal)፣ ሚስት ቤተሰብ ጋር (Matrilocal)፣ የባል እናት ወንድም/አጎት ጋር (Avunculocal)፣ በምርጫ (Ambilocal)፣ ወይም ራሳቸውን ችለው ለብቻ (Neolocal)። 💡 Exam Hint: የፐርሰንቴጆቹን ብዛት በደንብ ያዙ (Patrilocal 69% በመሆን አንደኛ ነው)! 📊 --- 3.7.2 Family * Family is the basis of human society. It is the most important primary group in society and a universal social institution. * Two fundamentally different types of family structure: 1. The Nuclear Family: Consisting of a married couple and their dependent children. Every adult belongs to two different nuclear families: * Family of Orientation: The family in which he/she was born and reared. * Family of Procreation: The family established through marriage. 2. The Extended Family: Consists of two or more nuclear families linked by blood ties living in a single household under a family head (~46% of societies per Murdock). 3.7.2.1 Functions of Marriage and Family 1. Biological Function: Regulates and socially validates long-term sexual relations and controls population reproduction. 2. Economic Function: Brings economic co-operation and division of labor based on sex and generation. 3. Social Function: Perpetuates family line and links kin groups. 4. Educational and Socialization Function: Enculturation, teaching values, and transmitting social heritage to children. 👉 Family of Orientation ማለት የተወለድንበት ቤተሰብ ሲሆን፤ Family of Procreation ደግሞ አግብተን የምንመሠርተው ቤተሰብ ነው። --- 3.7.3 Kinship * Kinship is social relations based on culturally recognized ties of descent and marriage. * Three ways kinship is created: 1. Consanguineous Kinship: Based on blood ties. 2. Affinal Kinship: Based on marriage relationships. 3. Fictitious Kinship: Based on adoption, fostering, or god-parenthood. 👉 የዘመድ አዝማድ ትስስር (Kinship) በ3 ይከፈላል፦ የደምና የሥጋ ዘመድ (Consanguineous)፣ የጋብቻ ዘመድ/አማች (Affinal)፣ እና በጉዲፈቻ/በእንጀራ አባት/እናት የሚመጣ (Fictitious)። --- 3.7.4 Descent * Descent Group: A permanent social unit whose members claim common ancestry. * Three important rules of descent: 1. Patrilineal Descent: Traced solely through the male line (sons continue affiliation; succession/inheritance passes through male line). 2. Matrilineal Descent: Traced solely through the female line (only females acquire succession and inheritance). 3. Cognatic Descent: Traced through either men or women without fixed rules. 👉 Descent (የትውልድ ሐረግ)፦ በአባት መስመር ብቻ (Patrilineal)፣ በእናት መስመር ብቻ (Matrilineal)፣ ወይም በሁለቱም እንደፈለጉ (Cognatic) ይቆጠራል። --- 3.8 Culture areas and culture contact * Culture area refers to a cluster of related cultures occupying a certain geographical region (concept introduced in 1920s by Alfred Kroeber). * In the context of Ethiopia, culture areas are relation to subsistence: 1. Plough Culture Area: Highland and central parts where agriculture is predominantly the backbone of the economy. Studied by ethnographers: Donald Levine, Allen Hobben, Fredrick Gamst, and Jack Bauer. 2. Enset Culture Area: Southern part of country (SNNPRS such as Guraghe, Sidama, Gedeo) where Enset serves as a staple diet. 3. Pastoral Culture Area: Lowland areas (Afar, Somali, Borena) relying on herds and cattle for a living with high mobility. 👉 በኢትዮጵያ 3 ዋና ዋና የባህል ቀጠናዎች (Culture Areas) አሉ፦ * Plough Culture Area (የእርሻ/የሞፈርና ቀንበር ባህል)፡ በደጋውና በመካከለኛው የኢትዮጵያ ክፍል። * Enset Culture Area (የእንሰት ባህል)፡ በደቡብ ኢትዮጵያ (ጉራጌ፣ ሲዳማ፣ ጌዴኦ)። * Pastoral Culture Area (የዘላን/የእንስሳት እርባታ ባህል)፡ በቆላማ ቦታዎች (አፋር፣ ሶማሌ፣ ቦረና)። 💡 Exam Hint: የኢትዮጵያን Culture Areas በሞፈር፣ በእንሰትና በዘላንነት ከፋፍላችሁ ያዙ! 🌾🐄 --- 3.9 Unit Summary * Culture consists of things people make, behavior, beliefs, and ideas. * Anthropology examines universals, generalities, and unique aspects using comparative perspective. * Avoid Ethnocentrism (believing one's culture is superior) and embrace Cultural Relativism (viewing cultures uniquely without superiority). * Culture change mechanisms: diffusion, acculturation, independent invention, and globalization. * Social ties (family, marriage, kinship) regulate relationships, residence, incest taboos, and descent rules. --- Dear EthioFresh Family, We hope this complete and comprehensive note makes your study time fun and effective!
